In my experience this place has had a hit or miss streak. We've been taking our dog here for quite some time now and in the times that her grooming was good, it was very good; in the times that it wasn't so good, it was easy to shrug off. This last time convinced us that it was time to find a new groomer. Last weekend, we brought our Australian Shepherd in for her usual mini-groom, and de-shedding. We always ask to add more detail when trimming her butt and legs and be sure to work out the knots that form around her face. We got none of this. When we picked up our dog, we were shocked to find that the groomer had obviously taken shortcuts and began shaving her in a very strange away. The fur around her face, and the fur on her lower back had all been improperly shaved without our knowledge or approval. It was clear just by looking at her that "working out knots" meant taking clippers to them and she looked horrible as a result, appearing more like a Lab rather than an Aussie. Even worse, there were parts he shaved we didn't even want them to touch including a weirdly shaped patch on her lower back, cutting away the curls she had and very nearly damaging her double coat. Ironically, one place he didn't touch was her belly which was just as long as when we brought her in. When we got her back in the car, she was shedding worse than she had ever done before leading us to assume that the de-shedding wasn't done, or not done properly. All of this for nearly $200. We got something we didn't want, and what they charged us for wasn't even complete. When we filed a complaint and asked for a refund, we were only given back $80 which felt more like an insult to what could have been a permanent issue to her double coat. Based off of our experience, I cannot suggest people bring their dogs here that require a bit more thought beyond a regular grooming. Their hit or miss record and the worst case scenario do not make the price tag worth the gamble.

My husky Shelby is 9 years old, and I’m not even going to lie… it had been WAY too long since she had been professionally groomed. Her coat was rough. I’m talking damn near sandpaper 😂. I knew she needed some serious attention.

The problem is my schedule is ridiculous. When I finally have an open day, I need somebody who can get me in NOW. I’m usually a same-day, walk-in type of customer because I genuinely don’t know what my availability is going to look like weeks in advance.

I called Woof Gang Bakery & Grooming. I knew about the location off Holcombe, but found out about the newer Heights location and gave them a shot.

They got Shelby in THE SAME DAY.

That alone was huge for me.

But the service? Man…

I gave them the most rough, vague instructions imaginable on how I wanted Shelby to look 😂 basically, “You see her… make her look good.”

THEY EXECUTED TO PERFECTION.

When I got my dog back, I could not believe it. Her coat feels completely different. She looks amazing. She seems happy. She’s walking around like she knows she’s fine now 😂😂😂.

No complaints. None.

They listened, understood exactly what I was trying to accomplish even when I probably did a terrible job explaining it, and absolutely nailed it.

This is the type of customer service that literally makes somebody’s day.

Shelby has officially found her groomer.

Five stars from me. I’ll be bringing my dog here from now on.

It seem like a silly thing that I write this review over $4.38, but the more I think about it the more annoyed I get. Yesterday, I decided to pick up a few treats for my dog. I decided on 3 yogurt peppermint heart shaped treats and 2 other things. The price stated $1.99/oz which means per ounce. When I looked at what was rung up as $1.99 each, I told the cashier it was by ounce and they looked over at the canister, then shrugged, and said 'It doesn't matter". I thought maybe they are 1 ounce per heart and the cashier had weighed them enough to know so I paid and went about my day. After I came home, out of curiosity, I used my kitchen scale to weigh all 3. They weren't even a whole ounce (.8 ounces to be exact) all together. So what should have been $1.59, I was charged $5.97. While there's nothing I can do about it now, I don't appreciate being over charged by triple in any circumstance or to be shrugged off when I have a genuine concern about my purchase.

What was most frustrating was that no apology or accountability was given. Being late can happen, but a simple apology and professionalism would have gone a long way.

Unfortunately, this is not the only issue I've had here. On another visit, I picked up my dog after about four hours. A couple hours later, I realized that her right eye was completely shut, her lashes were cut extremely short, and her eye was red and irritated. I ended up spending $178 on veterinary treatment for her eye.

I called the salon to report what happened and to simply understand whether something might have occurred during grooming (for example, shampoo getting in her eye or an accidental poke). No one ever called me back to address the issue or provide any explanation.

As a pet owner, I trust groomers with the care and safety of my dog. The lack of communication, accountability, and concern for my pet's well-being is unacceptable. I cannot recommend this place based on my experience.

From the moment I arrived, the groomer I was scheduled with had an immediate attitude and was rude right off the bat. The entire experience felt hostile, and honestly, it came across as microaggressive as well. When I picked up my dog, she was essentially shoved back into my arms with zero care or courtesy.

I will never return to this location or spend another dollar here, and I strongly advise others not to bring their pets—who deserve patience, kindness, and respect—to this business.

I had a very troubling second experience at Wolf Gang. After moving to the area recently, I carefully chose both a vet and a groomer for my two small dogs who are groomed every five weeks. Our first appointment went perfectly, and I truly thought I had found the right place.

However, for the second appointment—which I booked two weeks in advance—I dropped them off with the same instructions as always and asked for an ETA. As usual, I was told 2–3 hours. After four hours had passed with no update, I began calling to check on them. Five calls went straight to their generic voicemail before I was finally able to reach the on-duty manager. She told me that one dog was finished and the other still had another hour and a half to go—this was now 5.5 hours after drop-off.

When I asked why, she explained that one dog had an “accident,” which apparently caused a chain reaction of 5–6 other dogs also having accidents. I told her I’d never heard of something like that and asked normal clarifying questions—do the kennels have pee pads, liners, etc.? Her response was that my dog had been groomed, then soiled himself, and had to be groomed again.

I hung up and called a few veterinarian friends and groomers I know, all of whom said the story sounded suspicious and advised me to pick up my dogs immediately.

I called the manager back and told her I would be there in ten minutes. When I arrived, she repeated the same explanation—until the actual groomer came out and, right in front of her, said that wasn’t true. The real issue was that the original groomer had left, and there had clearly been a communication breakdown where no one realized my dog had been waiting for grooming. In other words, my dog was not “groomed twice” due to an accident—the manager’s story was simply untrue.

When I told the manager she had lied to me, she said that was “what she was told.” I said I expected to be compensated for the ordeal, and she offered a 10% discount. I declined and asked her to call the owner. She eventually contacted the on-call supervisor, but refused to let me speak with her. The supervisor allowed the manager to offer 15%, but again, would not speak with me directly.

For a groomer with a 4.9 rating, this entire situation was extremely unsettling. If it had not been for the honest groomer who told me what truly happened, I would never have known. Being lied to—especially about the care of your pets—is absolutely unacceptable.
